title: Smoothness of prime-to-characteristic Galois normalizations at separable branch points
statement:
Let $K$ be a field, $C$ a smooth integral $K$-curve, and $F=K(C)$. Let $L/F$ be a finite Galois extension of degree $d\geq1$, where finite Galois means finite-dimensional, normal and separable, and assume that the image of $d$ is invertible in $K$. Let $
u:Y	o C$ be the normalization of $C$ in $L$. Suppose $Y$ is a normal integral $K$-curve and $
u$ is finite. Let $D\subset C$ be a reduced closed subscheme finite etale over $K$, and suppose $
u$ is etale above $C\setminus D$. Then, for every $y\in Y$ above $x\in D$, the point $y$ is closed, the integer $[\kappa(y):\kappa(x)]$ divides $d$, and $\kappa(y)/K$ is finite separable. Moreover $Y	o\operatorname{Spec}K$ is smooth. Here normal means that every local ring is an integrally closed domain; separable means that minimal polynomials have no repeated roots. The field $K$ need not be perfect, no projectivity is required, and $D=\varnothing$ and $d=1$ are allowed.

Notions: [def-weil-field], [def-pc-curve], [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], [def-sc-function-field], [def-pc-field-extension], [def-fin-normalization-extension], [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], [def-weil-etale-morphism], [def-weil-closed-immersion], [def-weil-residue-field], [def-weil-vector-space-dimension].

source.place: Tag 09EB, lemma-galois-conclusion; varieties.tex Tag 0B8Y, lemma-regular-point-on-curve. Returned item proof steps 5--6: prime-to-characteristic residue degree, separability, and smoothness on and off the branch subscheme.

proof.text: First locate the branch points and their residue fields. Since $D\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ is finite, $D=\operatorname{Spec}H$ for a finite-dimensional $K$-algebra $H$. Its etaleness and [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-over-field-product] give $H\cong\prod_i K_i$ with each $K_i/K$ finite separable. Every point of this finite product spectrum is closed, with residue field one of the $K_i$. The closed immersion $D\hookrightarrow C$ takes it to a closed point $x$ of $C$ and induces $\kappa(x)\cong K_i$ by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-residue-field-iso]. Thus $\kappa(x)/K$ is finite separable. This argument also treats the empty product, when there is no branch point.

source.place: Tag 00U3, lemma-etale-over-field; morphisms.tex Tag 01WH, definition-integral; schemes.tex closed immersions and residue fields

proof.text: Fix $y\mapsto x\in D$ and an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}R\subset C$ containing $x$. Write $\mathfrak p\subset R$ for $x$. By [lem-sfb-curve-closed-point-affine-local-model], $\mathfrak p$ is maximal and $A=R_{\mathfrak p}\cong\mathcal O_{C,x}$ is a Noetherian local domain of dimension one, compatibly with $K$ and residue fields. By [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-scheme-over-field-regular], $A$ is regular, so [lem-sc-regular-dim1-dvr] makes $A$ a DVR. The affine function-field result gives $F=\operatorname{Frac}R$; also $\operatorname{Frac}A=F$, since $R\subset R_{\mathfrak p}\subset\operatorname{Frac}R$ and a quotient of two elements of $R$ is still a quotient of elements of $A$.

source.place: Tag 0B8Y, lemma-regular-point-on-curve, opening sentence; algebra.tex Tag 00PD, lemma-characterize-dvr, (3) implies (1); varieties.tex Tag 056S, lemma-smooth-regular

proof.text:
By the definition of normalization in $L$, $
u^{-1}U=\operatorname{Spec}B$ with $B$ the integral closure of $R$ in $L$; write $\mathfrak q\subset B$ for $y$. Finiteness of $
u$ says that $B$ is a finite $R$-module. The domain $B/\mathfrak q$ is therefore finite-dimensional over $R/\mathfrak p=\kappa(x)$, and is a field by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-dimensional-domain-is-field]. Hence $\mathfrak q$ is maximal and $y$ is closed in $
u^{-1}U$. Any specialization of $y$ in $Y$ maps to a specialization of the closed point $x$, hence lies over $x$ and is in $
u^{-1}U$. Consequently $y$ is closed in $Y$. Applying the affine local-model lemma to the curve $Y$ identifies $\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ with $B_{\mathfrak q}$, and identifies its residue field with that of $B_{\mathfrak q}$ compatibly with $K$.

source.place: Finite-dimensional domain criterion (rank-nullity); varieties.tex Tag 0B8Y, lemma-regular-point-on-curve, affine local rings; normalization affine description

proof.text: Put $S=R\setminus\mathfrak p$ and $T=S^{-1}B$. By [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-commutes-localization], $T$ is the integral closure of $A=S^{-1}R$ in $S^{-1}L=L$; the latter equality holds since all elements of $S$ are already nonzero units in $L$. The prime $\mathfrak n=S^{-1}\mathfrak q$ lies over the maximal ideal of $A$ and is maximal: $T/\mathfrak n=S^{-1}(B/\mathfrak q)=B/\mathfrak q$, a field, since every element of $S$ has nonzero image in that field. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-prime-residue-field-iso], $T_{\mathfrak n}\cong B_{\mathfrak q}$ and $\kappa(\mathfrak n)\cong\kappa(y)$, with the residue-field scalar maps induced from $R$ unchanged; likewise $\kappa(\mathfrak m_A)=\kappa(x)$. Apply [lem-sbc-dvr-galois-normalization-ramification-dvd] to the DVR $A$, its fraction field $F$, the finite Galois extension $L/F$, and $n=d=[L:F]$. It gives $f=[\kappa(y):\kappa(x)]\mid d$. No unramifiedness at $y$, perfection, or projectivity is used.

source.place: Tag 09EB, lemma-galois-conclusion; algebra.tex Tags 0307, lemma-integral-closure-localize, and 00E3, lemma-spec-localization

proof.text: Write $k=\kappa(x)$ and $E=\kappa(y)$. This extension is finite by the preceding step. The residue-normality theorem [lem-exc-dvr-residue-normal-action], applied to the same $A,L,T$ and $\mathfrak n$, says that $E/k$ is normal. If $\operatorname{char}K=p>0$, then $\operatorname{char}k=p$ and $p\nmid d$, because $K\hookrightarrow k$ is an inclusion of fields and $d$ is invertible in $K$. Choose an algebraic closure of $E$ using [lem-pc-algebraic-closure-exists-unique], and apply [lem-exc-normal-field-degree-factors] to $E/k$: for its relative separable closure $E_s$, $[E:k]=s[E:E_s]$ with $[E:E_s]=p^c$. Thus $p^c\mid f\mid d$, so $c=0$ and $[E:E_s]=1$. The nonzero element $1$ then spans the one-dimensional $E_s$-space $E$, giving $E=E_s$; by [def-weil-pbc-relative-separable-closure] $E/k$ is separable. In characteristic zero, any minimal polynomial $P$ over $k$ has positive degree $r$ and nonzero derivative: its leading derivative coefficient is $r$ times its nonzero leading coefficient. The irreducible derivative criterion [lem-trf-irreducible-separable-derivative] therefore makes every such $P$ separable. Thus in either characteristic $E/k$ is finite separable.

source.place: Tags 09HS, lemma-normal-and-automorphisms; 030L, definition-insep-degree; 09HI, lemma-finite-purely-inseparable; 09H0, lemma-irreducible-polynomials; more-algebra.tex Tag 09ED, lemma-galois-galois

proof.text: Step 1 gives $k/K$ finite separable and step 5 gives $E/k$ finite separable. By [lem-zl-separable-permanence], $E/K$ is separable algebraic, and by [lem-weil-pbc-field-degree-multiplicativity] it is finite, with $[E:K]=[E:k][k:K]$. Since $Y$ is a normal integral $K$-curve and $y$ is closed by step 3, [lem-sfb-normal-curve-separable-point-smooth] applies to $Y,y$: its local ring is integrally closed by the assumed normality, and its residue field is finite separable over $K$. Consequently $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ is smooth on some open neighbourhood of every point over $D$.

source.place: Tag 0B8Y, lemma-regular-point-on-curve; fields.tex Tags 09HB, lemma-separable-permanence, and 09G9, lemma-multiplicativity-degrees

proof.text:
For $z\in Y$ outside $
u^{-1}D$, use the assumed etaleness of $
u$ over $C\setminus D$. Since $C	o\operatorname{Spec}K$ is smooth at $
u(z)$, the pointwise assertion of [lem-trf-etale-source-smoothness] makes its composite with this etale restriction smooth at $z$. Together with step 6 this proves smoothness at every point of $Y$. The open smooth neighbourhoods supplied at these points cover $Y$, so the local definition of smoothness gives smoothness of its structure morphism. If $D$ is empty, this last argument applies everywhere; if $d=1$, the divisibility argument gives $f=1$ and all preceding steps remain valid.
